Class StatusScreen

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.tui.screen.StatusScreen
public class StatusScreen extends Object
TUI screen that displays the active status flags of all players in the current match. For each player, it shows their nickname in their pawn color and the list of currently active flags (such as hunt bonus, protection, discounts, and double shaman income), or a "no active flags" message if none are set. The screen blocks until the player presses Backspace to return to the previous view.

  • Method Details

    • display

      public void display() throws IOException
      Renders the status screen and blocks until the player presses Backspace. Saves and restores the terminal state and attributes around the display.
      Throws:
      IOException - if a terminal I/O error occurs

    • render

      public void render()
      Initializes the screen and color buffers to match the current terminal dimensions, writes the title and the status entry for each player into them, then flushes the result to the terminal. For each player, active flags are listed in green, separated by vertical bars; if none are active, a placeholder message is shown instead.

      Public so it can be re-invoked by the owning ViewTUI on a terminal resize while this screen is being displayed, keeping it visible and correctly sized instead of being silently replaced by a redraw of the main game layout.

    • waitForBackspace

      private void waitForBackspace()
      Blocks the current thread until the player presses Backspace (ASCII 8 or 127). Any other key press is ignored.

    • printAt

      private void printAt(int row, int col, String text, org.jline.utils.AttributedStyle style)
      Writes the given text into the screen and color buffers at the specified position, clipping any characters that fall outside the terminal width.
      Parameters:
      row - the zero-based row index to write at
      col - the zero-based column index to start writing from
      text - the text to write; ignored if null
      style - the ANSI style to apply to the written characters

    • flushBuffers

      private void flushBuffers()
      Flushes the screen and color buffers to the terminal. Clears any remaining content below the rendered area.
